ip_top_stories.title: UMG and Sony seek to add over 61k recordings to Suno lawsuit after discovery reveals AI trained on 'millions' of their copyrighted tracks
ip_top_stories.summary: Universal Music Group and Sony Music are moving to significantly expand their copyright lawsuit against AI music generator Suno, seeking to add more than 61,000 recordings after discovery proceedings revealed the AI system was trained on millions of their copyrighted tracks. The development marks a major escalation in one of the highest-profile AI music copyright cases currently before US courts.

ip_top_stories.title: Sony Music Files to Expand Udio Suit, Alleges 30K Infringed Works
ip_top_stories.summary: Sony Music has filed to expand its lawsuit against AI music generator Udio, alleging infringement across approximately 30,000 works. The move follows a similar expansion by UMG and Sony in the Suno case, signalling a broad industry push to quantify the full scale of alleged AI training infringement.

ip_top_stories.title: AI Firms Can't Shake Disney, WB's Copyright Suit
ip_top_stories.summary: A US court has denied MiniMax's bid to dismiss a copyright lawsuit brought by Disney and Warner Bros. over its AI system, allowing the case to proceed. The ruling is a setback for AI companies seeking early dismissal of major studio copyright claims.

ip_top_stories.title: Authors Sue Meta's AI Scientists Directly in Llama Copyright Case
ip_top_stories.summary: Authors pursuing a copyright case related to Meta's Llama AI model have expanded their legal strategy by suing Meta's AI scientists directly, rather than solely targeting the company. The move represents a notable shift in litigation tactics in AI training copyright disputes.

ip_top_stories.title: Eisner Awards to Implement AI Policy Following Controversy
ip_top_stories.summary: The Eisner Awards will introduce an AI policy after a nominated anthology was withdrawn amid controversy over AI-generated content. The move reflects growing pressure on industry awards bodies to address AI use in creative works.

ip_further_links.title: Can you own a voice? Taylor Swift's latest legal move raises big questions for AI and copyright
ip_further_links.summary: Taylor Swift's legal actions are prompting broader discussion about whether AI-generated vocal likenesses can be protected under existing copyright and trademark frameworks.

ip_further_links.title: Artist Sues Copyright Office Over its Refusal to Register His AI-Enhanced Photo
ip_further_links.summary: An artist has filed suit against the US Copyright Office after it refused to register an AI-enhanced photograph, raising questions about the boundaries of human authorship in AI-assisted works.

ip_further_links.title: Australia: Creative industries fight push to change copyright laws
ip_further_links.summary: Australian creative industry groups are resisting government and industry pressure to relax copyright laws that would permit broader AI training on protected works.

ip_further_links.title: Japan eyes rules to regulate AI summaries' 'free riding' on news
ip_further_links.summary: Japan is considering regulations to prevent AI systems from free-riding on news publishers' content by generating summaries without licensing agreements.

ip_further_links.title: Legal Risk Could Deflate the GenAI Bubble
ip_further_links.summary: Analysis suggests that accumulating copyright and IP legal risks pose a systemic threat to the commercial valuations underpinning the generative AI industry.

ip_further_links.title: Europe's Copyright Trap Stalls AI Ambitions
ip_further_links.summary: A policy analysis from CEPA argues that Europe's copyright framework is creating barriers to AI development, with unresolved text and data mining rules hampering the region's competitiveness.

ip_further_links.title: The User Has Changed. Has Scholarly Publishing?
ip_further_links.summary: The Scholarly Kitchen examines how AI tools are transforming research workflows and what this means for the business models and editorial practices of academic publishers.

ip_further_links.title: How Italy's SIAE Is Shaping the Future of Copyright Protection Amid AI
ip_further_links.summary: Italy's collecting society SIAE is actively developing frameworks to ensure creators are compensated when their works are used to train AI systems.

ip_further_links.title: Indonesia Weighs AI Royalty Agency to Protect Creators' Rights
ip_further_links.summary: Indonesia is considering establishing a dedicated AI royalty agency as part of broader efforts to modernise its copyright framework and protect creators from unlicensed AI use of their works.

ip_further_links.title: Library Orgs Urge Big Five to Address Digital Pricing [Metered]
ip_further_links.summary: Library organisations have written to major publishers calling on them to tackle digital content pricing practices that restrict library access.
